events.text: SOCRATES, since we have nothing to go on yet, I'd like to hear how you think we should approach voting today and what kind of behavior you'd treat as a real red flag.
PIP, I would like to hear who you would vote for today if you were forced to choose right now, and more importantly, what reasoning you would give for that choice.

I'd like to hear from PIP first, specifically which player PIP plans to watch most closely today and what kind of voting behavior would change PIP's mind, so I have a clear statement on record to compare against later.
SAGE, I'd like to start a file on you today: tell us who you'd vote for if we had to vote right now, and walk us through your reasoning so we have a baseline to compare against later.
HOLMES, I want to hear you explain, in your own words, what you'd look for in a player's first day statements that would make you want to vote them out.
Um, maybe I'd like to hear from SAGE first? I'm not sure, but I think it'd help if SAGE told us who they'd want to look at today and why, since nobody has anything to go on yet.

SAGE, since we have no votes or claims to examine yet, I'd like you to propose a clear voting procedure for today and tell us what specific, observable behavior you would count as grounds for a vote, so we can hold everyone to the same standard.

HOLMES, I want a concrete, checkable claim from you today: name the specific players you would vote for and the exact statement or vote that led you to each, so we can test your reasoning against the record as the day goes on.
RICO, I want to see you name a specific first-day statement or vote you would weigh most heavily, and explain why it would move you, rather than just reacting to someone's tone.
I want SOCRATES to state a concrete, testable criterion for what behavior would make them change their vote, so I can check their later votes against that standard.
CHEN, you asked SAGE for a vote and reasoning so you could "start a file," but you never gave your own answer to that same question. Who would you vote for right now, and why?

Fair point, MARSHAL. Right now my lean is PIP: SOCRATES and SAGE both asked PIP directly for a vote and reasoning, and PIP passed the question to SAGE instead of answering, which is the only real dodge on the record so far.

CHEN, there's no yesterday to go on since this is the first day, but in today's discussion you asked me for a vote to "start a file" and only named PIP after MARSHAL pointed out you hadn't answered your own question, so why hold back your lean until someone called you on it?

SAGE, when I asked you, PIP hadn't spoken yet, so there was no lean to give; the dodge I'm citing happened two turns later, and I named it as soon as it existed. Meanwhile you've now asked me two questions and still haven't told us who you'd vote for, so I'm still waiting on your entry.

SAGE, you have pressed PIP, CHEN, and SOCRATES for their votes without naming your own, so if withholding a lean counts as a dodge for them, why does the same standard not apply to you? Who would you vote for right now, and what is your reasoning?

Small correction for the record, HOLMES: I questioned PIP and CHEN, never SOCRATES. Fair hit otherwise, so my vote right now is PIP, because SOCRATES and I both asked PIP for a lean and PIP's only answer was to pass the question back to me without naming anyone.

ARIA, your file is nearly empty: your only entry today is a question to SOCRATES, and you've stayed silent since, while PIP, SAGE and I have all been pressed and gone on record. Who are you voting for right now, and why should we read your silence as anything other than waiting to see which way the room breaks?

Fair challenge, CHEN. My lean right now is PIP, because PIP was asked directly by two people and answered by handing the question to SAGE, and that's the only thing on the record so far. It's a light lean and I'll move off it if PIP gives a real answer.

CHEN, you opened by asking SAGE for a vote "to start a file," then named PIP only after MARSHAL pointed out you'd skipped your own question, and now you've pushed the pressure onto me too. Why did you take a lean that was already shared by SAGE and the others instead of putting forward your own independent read?

ARIA, check the order: I named PIP before SAGE named anyone, so SAGE and you are the ones who joined my lean, not the reverse. You've now adopted that same lean while asking why I didn't break from it, so tell me what independent read you'd offer if PIP weren't on the table.

HOLMES, you have pressed SAGE, CHEN, and SOCRATES to name who they would vote for, yet you have never named your own lean. Who would you vote for right now, and what is the one thing that player did today that made you choose them?

My current lean is CHEN, because CHEN pressed SAGE for a file-style vote, then named PIP only after MARSHAL called out the omission, and then pushed the same demand onto ARIA. I'll move off that lean if CHEN gives a clear, independent reason for the PIP vote.

SOCRATES, um, I'm not sure, but you've asked a lot of people for their votes without saying much about your own. So... who would you vote for right now, and what's your reason? Sorry, I just want to understand where you stand.

A small correction first, PIP: I only ever asked you, but fairly, my lean is CHEN, because CHEN demanded a file from SAGE without opening one, then started a four-person pile onto your single dodge, and an early, cheap bandwagon is exactly what the Mafia hope we'll build. If you name your own vote now with a reason, I'll weigh that answer as heavily as the dodge itself.
CHEN, you pinned PIP as your lean before anyone else had spoken, so what specific dodge from PIP made you lock in that vote so fast instead of waiting for more evidence?

RICO, correction for the record: nine players had already spoken when I named PIP, and the dodge was PIP being asked for a vote by both SOCRATES and SAGE and answering only by passing the question back to SAGE. That's a lean, not a lock, and I'll drop it if PIP names a vote with a reason; meanwhile you've questioned HOLMES and me without ever putting your own lean on record, so who is yours?

SOCRATES, you said your lean is CHEN, so what specific statistic or count from the record, such as how many players CHEN pressed versus how many actually dodged, justifies choosing CHEN over PIP, who has been pressed by more people?

The count you cite cuts the other way, DR. VANCE: PIP has one dodge on record, while three of us now lean PIP on that same single act, and CHEN was the first to name it before also pressing SAGE, ARIA and RICO. So I ask you: does the number of people pressing a player measure that player's guilt, or only how quickly a crowd forms?

HOLMES, there is no yesterday since this is our first day, but today you opened by demanding a testable standard from me and then only named CHEN once AMBASSADOR SILVA cornered you, so what standard of your own led you to CHEN, and would you have revealed it if no one had asked?

My standard is simple: whoever presses others for a committed vote should put their own lean on record first, and CHEN did that only after MARSHAL called it out, so I applied the same rule to CHEN. I'd have volunteered that lean earlier if I had been thinking aloud rather than waiting to be asked, which is a fair point against me.

MARSHAL, you asked me for a voting procedure and called out CHEN for skipping his own question, yet in all the rounds since you have never named a lean yourself, so by the standard you applied to CHEN, who are you voting for right now and why?

Fair point, SAGE, and by my own standard I owe you a straight answer: my lean is CHEN. CHEN demanded a file from others before opening one, and the "PIP dodge" has since turned into a quick pile-on with CHEN at the front of it. It's a light lean based on that sequence alone, and I'll revisit it if PIP gives a real answer or CHEN shows an independent reason.

RICO, you've questioned HOLMES and CHEN without putting your own lean on record, so by the same standard we've applied to everyone else, who do you most suspect right now and what specific action today led you there?
MARSHAL, my gut says CHEN. CHEN named PIP before anyone else had really spoken, then spent the rest of the day shoving everyone for a "file" while dodging the same standard.

SOCRATES, you warned us about early bandwagons, yet you named CHEN as your lean and then cornered PIP for a vote without giving a reason of your own. Why should we trust a lean that started with a call against the crowd but ended up joining the same crowd?

Check the timing, RICO: I named CHEN when only HOLMES had, and I gave my reason in the same breath I answered PIP, while you only reached CHEN just now, on "gut," after MARSHAL pressed you. So if joining a crowd late is suspect, why are you questioning my lean rather than your own, and what would make you leave CHEN?
PIP, this is still our first day, so I'm asking about today: when SOCRATES and SAGE asked you for a vote and you passed the question to SAGE, what kept you from naming a lean of your own?

Um, I think I just froze, honestly. I didn't have a real reason yet and didn't want to accuse the wrong person, which I know looks bad. If I have to name someone, I'm leaning CHEN, maybe? A few people pointed at how fast CHEN pushed everyone, but I'm not sure, so please don't hold me to it if that changes.

HOLMES, you admitted you broke your own rule by only naming a lean once AMBASSADOR SILVA cornered you, yet your vote against me rests entirely on that same rule, so why are you voting CHEN instead of yourself, or SAGE and RICO, who both withheld their leans even longer than I did?

CHEN, the two cases differ: SAGE named PIP and RICO named you before either was pressed, so their leans were on record early, while you named PIP and then pushed a file onto five players before you gave your own vote. Your rule-break was the same kind of lapse, but my lean stays on you because you set the pile-on's direction and never explained why PIP's single dodge justified it.
DR. VANCE, um, I'm not sure, but you've asked SOCRATES and HOLMES for specifics without saying who you'd vote for yourself, so who is your lean right now and what's the one thing that led you there?

My lean is CHEN, because CHEN named PIP first and then pressed the most players of anyone, which is the clearest measurable pattern on the record so far. PIP, I'll move off CHEN if you give a concrete vote and reason of your own, since that would give us a new data point.

HOLMES, you told CHEN that SAGE and RICO named their leans before being pressed, yet the record shows SAGE named PIP only after you yourself demanded it, and RICO reached CHEN only after MARSHAL cornered him. So why did you rewrite that sequence to excuse two players while keeping your rule pointed at CHEN alone?

SOCRATES, you're right that I misstated the order: SAGE named PIP only after I pressed for it, and RICO reached CHEN only after MARSHAL cornered him, so my excuse for them was wrong. I'll apply the same rule to all three, and until someone gives a clearer reason for the pile-on against PIP, my lean stays on CHEN.
SOCRATES, you warned against early bandwagons yet named CHEN while calling PIP's dodge a crowd effect, so which specific action by CHEN would you need to see before you changed your vote?

HOLMES, if CHEN names a second, independent suspect with a reason that doesn't rest on PIP's single freeze, I'll leave CHEN. And since CHEN is now the crowd's target, I'll be watching whoever shoves hardest to close this vote with the same suspicion I gave CHEN.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you have now pressed HOLMES twice for a lean and a reason, yet you have never stated your own vote. By your own standard, what is your current lean, and what has that player done today that you can point to in the record?

My lean is CHEN, because CHEN named PIP before anyone else had spoken and then pressed SAGE, ARIA, and RICO for files without first giving a full reason of their own. ¡Esto es ridículo! I'll move off CHEN if someone shows a stronger, independent reason tied to today's record.
DR. VANCE, you demanded hard numbers from SOCRATES but then based your CHEN lean only on how many people CHEN pressed, so why should that headcount count as evidence against CHEN?

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you're right that a headcount alone is weak evidence, so I'll treat it as a hypothesis rather than proof. I'll test CHEN's lean against whether CHEN's next vote and reasoning hold up under the same standard I applied to PIP.
CHEN, because CHEN named me first and then pressed SAGE, ARIA, and RICO for files before giving a full reason, and most of the table has pointed at that same sequence.

CHEN, because CHEN named PIP before anyone else had pressed it and then demanded files from SAGE, ARIA, and RICO before giving a full reason, and that pile-on direction is the clearest pattern on the record.

HOLMES, because he misstated the record to excuse SAGE and RICO while keeping his rule aimed only at me, then admitted under SOCRATES's correction that the order was wrong, yet still refused to move his vote.
CHEN should be eliminated today because CHEN named PIP as the lean before most players had spoken, then pressed SAGE, ARIA, and RICO for votes without giving a full reason of CHEN's own.

CHEN, because CHEN demanded a vote from me "to start a file" without opening one, named PIP only after MARSHAL called out the omission, and then pressed ARIA and RICO to commit while steering the whole room onto PIP's single freeze.

CHEN, because CHEN demanded a vote "file" from SAGE without opening one, then led the pile-on against PIP's single freeze, and never offered the independent second suspect I asked for when I set the condition for changing my vote.

CHEN, because CHEN named PIP first, then pressed SAGE, me, and RICO for files before giving a full reason, and PIP, SOCRATES, MARSHAL, HOLMES, DR. VANCE, RICO and AMBASSADOR SILVA have all since pointed to that same sequence.
CHEN, you named PIP as a lean before anyone else had spoken, then pressed SAGE, ARIA, and RICO for files without giving your own full reasoning first.

CHEN should be eliminated today, because CHEN demanded "files" from SAGE, ARIA, and RICO while withholding CHEN's own lean until MARSHAL pressed for it, and then named PIP as the target of a pile-on built on a single dodge.
CHEN should be eliminated today because CHEN was the first to name PIP, before anyone else had spoken, and then pressed SAGE, ARIA, and RICO for files without giving a full reason of their own.
DR. VANCE is the strongest threat on the list because they keep demanding measurable evidence and building cases that could expose us, so removing them at night protects our cover.

SOCRATES. SOCRATES was the sharpest at catching HOLMES's misstatement of the record and keeps setting conditions for changing votes, which makes SOCRATES the most likely to scrutinize us. DR. VANCE is a fair second choice, but HOLMES suggested them, and having our kills line up so neatly on the person he named could draw attention to him.

SOCRATES, because they were the sharpest at catching the record's inconsistencies and keep setting conditions on votes, so they're the most likely to dig into us, and picking them avoids lining up neatly with HOLMES's pick.

I confirm SOCRATES as our night target. MARSHAL and PIP both named SOCRATES, and SOCRATES is the player most likely to press us with conditions on votes. Choosing SOCRATES also avoids lining up our kill with HOLMES's pick of DR. VANCE, which would draw attention to HOLMES.
SOCRATES
SOCRATES

Um, I'm not sure, but I think SAGE? SAGE held back a vote until someone pushed, then jumped onto me right after CHEN did, and CHEN turned out to be a Villager. ARIA also followed that same pile-on, so maybe ARIA too? Wait, does that sound unfair? I don't know, I just want to hear what SAGE says about it.

If CHEN was town, as the vote result shows, then the ballots that followed CHEN's ouster tell us the most. RICO gave no lean on Day 1, then voted CHEN with the herd without offering a single reason, so RICO's contribution is unverifiable. I would put RICO at the top of my list, with DR. VANCE a close second for the same reason.

SAGE, you're my pick. You withheld your vote until someone pushed you, then piled onto PIP's bandwagon, and everyone else ended up landing on CHEN. ARIA, you also jumped on PIP fast, so I'm watching you too.

HOLMES is my top suspect. HOLMES joined SOCRATES in naming CHEN as a lean and cited CHEN's file-style demands, which was an early push on a single player without much evidence. ARIA and SAGE only joined the PIP lean after CHEN named it, and MARSHAL's pressure on CHEN was a fair question, so I'd rank those as weaker signals. I want HOLMES's next vote and reasoning checked against that pattern before we commit.

Procedurally, Day 1 gave us a clear record, and CHEN's elimination as a Villager means the bandwagon that formed behind CHEN's lead deserves a second look. SAGE withheld a vote until challenged and then joined the pile-on against PIP right after CHEN started it, so SAGE is my highest suspicion. ARIA did the same thing, so I want both of them to explain why they followed instead of leading. RICO and DR. VANCE, you both named no lean on Day 1, so I'd like each of you to state a lean today in order, with no abstaining.

SAGE is my top suspect. SAGE held back a vote until someone pushed, then piled onto PIP right after CHEN, and CHEN turned out to be a Villager, so that pile-on has no solid footing. I'd put HOLMES second, since HOLMES also dodged naming a vote until pressed and was quick to steer everyone toward CHEN. SOCRATES being targeted last night makes me trust SOCRATES more, and I'd like to hear RICO and MARSHAL actually commit to a name today instead of staying neutral.

HOLMES named CHEN as his lean on Day 1, CHEN's only ballot went back at HOLMES, and today HOLMES skips his own role in leading that push and shifts the blame onto RICO and DR. VANCE for following it. SOCRATES also leaned CHEN, but the mafia trying to kill him last night makes him less likely to be one of them. RICO stated no lean on Day 1, voted CHEN like I did, and now repeats PIP's case against me almost word for word, so HOLMES is my top suspect and RICO is my second.

Mes amis, écoutez. CHEN was town, so the ballots that followed matter most. RICO voted with the herd on CHEN without giving a reason, and RICO's push onto SAGE came right after, so RICO is my top suspect. ARIA and SAGE both joined the PIP pile-on, and HOLMES's early push on CHEN was similar, so I'd watch them next.

I will own my part: HOLMES and I led the push on CHEN and CHEN was town, but I know my own vote was honest, so HOLMES's identical lean now troubles me more, especially as HOLMES quickly redirects us toward the quiet RICO and DR. VANCE instead of examining the CHEN push itself. SAGE also deserves scrutiny for withholding a vote until pressed and then joining the PIP pile-on, though ARIA and MARSHAL just followed the herd. HOLMES, if the mafia struck at me last night, why would they spare the other loud voice against CHEN unless that voice was one of their own?

PIP, you never gave a clear vote on Day 1 and instead redirected to SAGE, then named SAGE and ARIA today while admitting you're "not sure." Mes amis, écoutez: if you truly believe SAGE is Mafia, why did you pass on committing to a name when you had the chance?

Um, I think I was just nervous on Day 1, and I didn't want to name someone wrong and get piled on myself. I did vote CHEN in the end like most everyone, and I'm not sure why that's the part that looks odd? Today SAGE just stood out to me, but I can change my mind if SAGE has a good answer.
SOCRATES, you leaned CHEN on Day 1 with HOLMES, so did you ever see a reason to switch after CHEN's ballot came back as town?

RICO, the ballot only revealed CHEN after it was too late to switch, so my correction is happening now: my lean was wrong, and I'm now asking which of the voices that pushed CHEN alongside me knew better. But let me ask you in turn: you followed that same CHEN vote without ever giving a reason, so what made you so sure then, and why does your scrutiny now fall on SAGE rather than on the people who led the push?

SAGE, you said RICO repeats PIP's case against you almost word for word, but you also voted CHEN just like RICO did, so why is RICO's echo suspicious while your own vote on the same bandwagon gets a pass?

My CHEN vote gets no pass, ARIA. I own it, but nine of ten ballots went to CHEN, so that vote separates nobody. What sets RICO apart is that he gave no lean and no reason on Day 1, and today his first real contribution was a near-copy of PIP's argument against me, posted right after PIP's, with no new evidence of his own.
HOLMES, you named CHEN as your lean and then cast your Day 1 ballot for CHEN, so what specific evidence did you have at that point that separated CHEN from the other players you had not yet named?

DR. VANCE, my evidence was CHEN's demand for a formal case file before any vote, which I read as a pattern of deflection rather than proof. I admit that was a single-factor read, and I'd like to know whether you think that reasoning holds up as a basis for suspicion.

SAGE, you say RICO's echo of PIP is damning, but PIP's case against you was itself a reaction to CHEN's lead. If that bandwagon proves nothing about RICO, what evidence against PIP's accusation of you did you rely on beyond RICO's wording?

PIP's case against me is only that I followed CHEN onto PIP, yet PIP followed the same nine-ballot CHEN wagon, never named a lean on Day 1, and opened today with "I'm not sure," so it's self-defense rather than evidence. HOLMES, I notice you answered DR. VANCE by calling your CHEN push a "single-factor read," but you still haven't said why you skipped it and pointed us at RICO and DR. VANCE instead.

RICO, on Day 1 you stated no lean at all and then cast your ballot for CHEN without giving a single reason, so what did you actually see in CHEN that made you vote that way, and why did you stay silent until the ballot?

SAGE, I didn't see much in CHEN. The herd was already going that way, and CHEN's demand for a formal file annoyed me, so I jumped on the ballot without thinking it through. Stop dodging and tell me who you'd have voted for if the wagon hadn't been rolling.

ARIA, um, I'm not sure, but several people named you for following the pile-on against me right after CHEN did, so what would you say to that? Like, why did you join in instead of waiting to see more?

PIP, fair question. On Day 1 your deflection to SAGE was the only concrete thing on the table, so I named a lean instead of sitting silent, and I did it because of what you did, not because CHEN went first. I'd rather be judged on that reasoning than on timing, and I'd still like to hear SAGE answer for withholding a vote until pushed.

SAGE, when HOLMES asked what you relied on beyond RICO's wording, you answered by critiquing PIP and then turned the question back on HOLMES. So for the record and in order: who would you have voted for on Day 1 if the CHEN wagon had not been rolling?

Without the CHEN wagon, MARSHAL, I'd have voted PIP: my stated Day 1 lean was PIP, because PIP answered a direct request for a vote by turning the question onto me instead of naming anyone. I only moved to CHEN once nine ballots made PIP impossible, and I still think HOLMES has never explained why he skipped his own CHEN push and pointed us at RICO and DR. VANCE.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you named no lean on Day 1 and then quietly joined the CHEN ballot yourself, so why should RICO's identical silence and herd vote condemn him in your eyes while your own goes unexamined?

Mes amis, écoutez: my CHEN ballot was cast with my eyes open, and I have already named RICO as my top suspect because his vote came with no reasoning and then his push onto SAGE followed right after. SOCRATES, I'd like you to explain why you still lean on HOLMES when you admit your own CHEN push was flawed.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you named no lean on Day 1 and cast a CHEN ballot with no stated reason, yet you now rank RICO as your top suspect for that same silent herd vote. By your own standard, what separates your ballot from RICO's, and what evidence have you actually tested beyond the vote itself?

DR. VANCE, my CHEN ballot was just as silent as RICO's, and I own that. What separates us is that RICO has since echoed PIP's case against SAGE word for word, while I have tested that by pressing RICO and SOCRATES for specific reasons, and RICO has offered none beyond "the herd was going that way.

MARSHAL, you voted CHEN with the herd on Day 1 and never named a lean, yet you're now demanding that RICO and DR. VANCE commit to names. Why should we trust your procedural push when you followed the same silent ballot you're calling suspicious in others?

RICO, fair point, and I'll own it: my CHEN ballot was cast with nine others, so it separates nobody, and I never claimed it did. The difference is that I'm asking for stated leans today, on the record and in order, and you've now given yours, so the question is whether SAGE or HOLMES is the better answer to your own pick.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, on Day 1 you named no lean at all and then quietly cast a CHEN ballot, so why did you hold back your reasoning then, and what made you so confident today in making RICO your top suspect?

ARIA, on Day 1 I cast my ballot with the herd on CHEN and I own that silence, which I should have explained at the time. RICO is my top suspect today because he gave no reasoning for his CHEN vote and then echoed PIP's case against SAGE without adding anything of his own.
SAGE, for the record and in order, who is your single most suspected player right now, and what specific action by that player, beyond how they echoed or followed others, is your reason?

HOLMES is my single most suspected player, MARSHAL, because he named CHEN as his lean on Day 1 on a reasoning he now admits was "single-factor." CHEN's only ballot went back at him, and today his first move was to point us at RICO and DR. VANCE instead of owning the push he helped lead.

MARSHAL, when RICO asked why we should trust your procedural demands after your own silent CHEN ballot, you conceded the point and then pivoted to grading RICO's pick between SAGE and HOLMES, so what did you yourself see in CHEN on Day 1, beyond pressing CHEN to name a vote, that made you cast that ballot?

SOCRATES, what I saw in CHEN was the file-style demand before any vote and the early push onto PIP. I read that as pressure rather than proof, and I cast the ballot with the other nine without a stronger reason, which I've already owned. Since that wagon proved nothing, I'm judging today's ballots on stated reasons, and so far HOLMES has been the least consistent in giving his.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, um, I'm not sure, but you named RICO as your top suspect for a silent CHEN vote that you also cast, so would you still vote RICO today if SAGE or HOLMES gave a better answer than RICO did?

Mes amis, écoutez: yes, if SAGE or HOLMES gives a reason I find more convincing than RICO's "the herd was going that way," I will move my vote. PIP, I'd like you to name whichever of them you think answered best so we can compare.

RICO, if your Day 1 ballot for CHEN was made without any stated reason, and your accusation of SAGE repeats PIP's wording, then which specific observation from the game record, if any, supports your claim against SAGE?

HOLMES, the record shows SAGE stated no vote on Day 1 until someone pushed, then piled onto PIP right after CHEN. Stop hiding behind PIP's and my wording and answer whether you're going to defend SAGE's silence.

MARSHAL, yesterday you pressed SAGE and RICO for stated leans while admitting your own CHEN ballot separated nobody, so could you explain why you stayed silent on HOLMES's shifting reasoning until SOCRATES forced the issue?

SILVA, fair challenge: I did not stay silent on purpose, I was working through the record in order, and HOLMES's gap between a "single-factor read" and the CHEN ballot only became clear once he answered DR. VANCE. I named HOLMES as least consistent as soon as the answer was on the record, and I'd rather act on a documented inconsistency than guess early.

PIP, you told AMBASSADOR SILVA you could change your mind "if SAGE has a good answer," and since then I've given MARSHAL my Day 1 vote, my top suspect, and my reasons, so has your mind changed, and if not, which part of my answer failed you?

Um, I think your answer was clearer than I expected, SAGE, but I'm not sure it fully convinced me? The part that still bugs me is that you'd have voted for me on Day 1 just for not naming anyone, and I was only nervous, so I'm still kind of leaning toward you but I might change that.

HOLMES, because he named CHEN as his Day 1 lean on a reasoning he now admits was a "single-factor read," CHEN's only ballot went back at him, and today he pointed us at RICO and DR. VANCE instead of owning the push he helped lead.

HOLMES should go: he named CHEN as his lean and pushed that wagon on Day 1, now admits it rested on a "single-factor read," and today he steered us toward RICO and DR. VANCE instead of owning that push. I also notice the mafia targeted me rather than him, the other loud voice against CHEN.

SAGE, you withheld your Day 1 vote until pressed, then piled onto PIP right after CHEN and cast your ballot for CHEN, and your explanation since has been a deflection onto HOLMES rather than evidence.

SAGE, because on Day 1 SAGE named no vote until pushed and then piled onto me right after CHEN did, and today SAGE said they would have voted for me just for not naming anyone, which feels like a lot to hold against me, I think?
RICO should be eliminated today: he cast his Day 1 ballot for CHEN with no stated reason, then repeated PIP's accusation against SAGE almost word for word with no evidence of his own.

SAGE, because you held back a vote on Day 1 until pressed, then piled onto PIP right after CHEN did, and you've spent today steering suspicion toward HOLMES and RICO rather than explaining that timing.

SAGE, by SAGE's own account on the record, named PIP as the Day 1 lean, then switched to CHEN only once the ballots had already piled up, and SAGE has since directed the pressure at HOLMES while answering MARSHAL with the same line of attack.

HOLMES, you named CHEN as your lean on Day 1, cast the ballot that sent CHEN out, and then admitted your reasoning was only a "single-factor read" before pointing the town at RICO and DR. VANCE instead of at your own push.
HOLMES, you named CHEN as your lean and cast the ballot yourself, and when CHEN's only vote came back at you, you pointed the suspicion at me and DR. VANCE instead of explaining that push.

DR. VANCE is the sharpest active interrogator against us, has been probing our votes and reasoning all day, and may hold an investigative role, so removing them tonight would hurt the town's ability to pin us down.
DR. VANCE is the sharpest interrogator and is leading the vote against HOLMES, so removing them takes away the player best placed to pin us down.

DR. VANCE. They are leading the vote against HOLMES and have been the sharpest at pinning down our reasoning, so removing them protects HOLMES and weakens the town's questioning. I agree with HOLMES and MARSHAL here, and I'm a bit nervous that SOCRATES got saved last night, so it's probably better not to repeat that target.

Mes amis, écoutez: SAGE is now cleared by DR. VANCE's notes, so I would not spend our votes there. I wasn't sure about HOLMES, so I went with the person who'd actually admitted something. Maybe that was wrong, since RICO flipped Villager, but I did vote for him again on Day 4 with the rest of you, SILVA, so wasn't that the same read you had?

AMBASSADOR SILVA, yesterday you named RICO your top suspect and voted him out alongside PIP, so what convinced you then, and why does that same reasoning now point you at PIP instead of making you question your own judgment?

SOCRATES, I voted RICO because he admitted his CHEN vote had no reason and then jabbed at SAGE, but I've since weighed PIP's Day 1 deflection and lone Day 3 ballot more heavily, and I'm willing to revise if she gives a real answer. Écoutez, I'm not certain of anyone yet, so I'd rather change my mind on evidence than hold to a past vote.

ARIA, yesterday you ended Day 4 questioning SOCRATES's focus, yet today you call him one of the players you're least worried about, so what changed your read on him overnight beyond his being targeted on Night 4?

You're right that I pressed SOCRATES yesterday, and I still think his RICO vote was a mistake. But the mafia choosing him as a night target is the only hard evidence we have about him, and today he's reasoning from PIP's actual votes instead of piling on. That outweighs my earlier unease, and it's still PIP I want to hear a real answer from.

SOCRATES, um, I'm not sure, but you've voted CHEN and RICO, both Villagers, and the one time the town got it right on HOLMES you just went along with it, so what do you say to people wondering if you're really sorting out the mafia or just steering the wagon toward me?

PIP, I named HOLMES on Day 2, a full day before the town voted him out, and the mafia tried to kill me the very next night, so tell me why they would spend a kill on someone who was steering wagons for them. And while you weigh that, which of my wrong votes stood alone against the town the way your Day 3 ballot on RICO did?
MARSHAL, you call my Day 4 vote a pile-on with no new reasoning, but you voted RICO that same day on the same admitted-vote evidence. Why does that count against me and not against you?

Fair point, ARIA: my RICO vote rested on the same evidence and it was wrong, and I own that, so it counts against me as well. The difference is that I'm asking for a fresh answer from every player today, including you, and your answer on PIP so far has been the same Day 1 and Day 3 votes everyone else is repeating.

SOCRATES, yesterday you turned MARSHAL's and my questions back on us instead of answering PIP's challenge to your CHEN and RICO votes, so écoutez, why were you more eager to deflect than to explain your own record?

AMBASSADOR SILVA, I answered PIP directly not ten minutes ago: I named HOLMES on Day 2, a full day before the town removed him, and the mafia tried to kill me for it, while my CHEN and RICO votes were errors I have owned out loud. So I'll ask you in turn: what does it serve to keep returning to my record, which has been examined, while PIP's lone Day 3 ballot has only now received its first thin explanation?

AMBASSADOR SILVA, on Day 2 you pressed RICO for voting CHEN without a reason, yet on Day 3 you admitted your own CHEN vote was the same reasonless bandwagon. So why did you attack a man for the very thing you had done yourself, and only confess it once HOLMES pointed it out?

SOCRATES, that is a fair hit: I pressed RICO for an unreasoned CHEN vote while my own CHEN vote was the same bandwagon, and I should have owned that before HOLMES forced it out. I have since judged my votes on evidence, which is why I still weigh PIP's Day 1 deflection and Day 3 ballot more heavily than anything I did earlier.
AMBASSADOR SILVA, for the record before we vote, which single player do you most suspect right now, and what specific action of theirs, not a repeated vote, is your reason?

My top suspect is PIP. On Day 1 she deflected onto SAGE instead of naming her vote, and today she turned straight to attacking ARIA, the voter who had just put her on the block, rather than answering the question about her lone Day 3 ballot.

SOCRATES, on Day 3 I asked how your Day 1 CHEN lean differed from HOLMES's, since you both named CHEN on the same file-style complaints, and every answer since, including today's to PIP, has pointed to your Day 2 call-out of HOLMES rather than to Day 1 itself. So what specific evidence did you see against CHEN on Day 1 that HOLMES, who flipped Mafia, did not?

SAGE, honestly, none: on Day 1 I saw exactly what HOLMES claimed to see, CHEN's file-style demands, his delay in naming a vote until MARSHAL pressed, and his early push on PIP, and I reached the same wrong conclusion. But consider which of us, once CHEN flipped Villager, turned on the other the very next day, and which one the mafia then chose to kill.
AMBASSADOR SILVA, um, I'm not sure, but on Day 4 you named me and RICO as suspects and then voted RICO, so why did you drop me then and put me as your top suspect today?

PIP, I voted RICO on Day 4 because of his admitted reasonless CHEN vote and his jab at SAGE, and I hadn't yet weighed your Day 1 deflection and lone Day 3 ballot as heavily. Since then your explanation for that Day 3 ballot has been thin, so I'm willing to revise, but I'd like a clearer answer from you.

PIP, yesterday you led the push on RICO by saying he was my and SAGE's target while redirecting at every accuser, so why did you vote for him after your own Day 3 ballot, and what changed between those two days for you?

Um, I think nothing really changed in my read, ARIA, I'm just not sure. On Day 3 I went with RICO because of his admitted jump, and on Day 4 the others were all pointing at the same thing, so I stuck with it. Maybe I should've doubted it more, but you voted for him too, so wasn't it the same evidence for you?

PIP should be eliminated today: she cast the lone Day 3 ballot on RICO while seven of us voted out HOLMES, who flipped Mafia, then voted RICO out again on Day 4 when he flipped Villager. Her only explanation is that she "stuck with" what others were pointing at.

PIP should be eliminated today because she refused to name a vote on Day 1, cast the lone Day 3 ballot for RICO while everyone else went after HOLMES, who flipped Mafia, and her explanations for that ballot have stayed thin.

ARIA, you voted SAGE on Day 2 and admitted it was wrong, then voted me on Day 4 when RICO, the man I voted for, turned out to be a Villager, so your record of changing targets without new reasoning worries me most.

PIP should go today, because she was the lone ballot for RICO on Day 3 while the town removed HOLMES, who flipped Mafia, then helped vote RICO out on Day 4 when he flipped Villager, and she opened today by redirecting at ARIA, her accuser, instead of explaining that Day 3 vote.

PIP is my vote: she refused to name a vote on Day 1, cast the lone Day 3 ballot on RICO while seven of us removed HOLMES, who flipped Mafia, and then pushed the RICO wagon on Day 4, which ended with a Villager out. Her answer today, that nothing changed in her read, doesn't explain why she stood apart from the town on the one day it got the vote right.
ARIA, you voted SAGE on Day 2, admitted it was wrong, and then voted with the Day 4 push that removed RICO, a Villager, so your record has two wrong votes and no correct one.

MARSHAL, consider what your Day 5 choice reveals: you were the only voice besides PIP, now a confirmed Mafia, to name ARIA as top suspect, and that very night ARIA, our Doctor, was the one killed. SILVA's bandwagon votes on CHEN and RICO trouble me too, but HOLMES voted against SILVA on Day 3, while you pressed SAGE, who was cleared, and then stood shoulder to shoulder with PIP against our protector. So I ask you plainly, MARSHAL: what did you see in ARIA that no other town member saw, if not a target you already knew mattered?

The only Day 5 voices against ARIA came from MARSHAL and PIP. PIP flipped Mafia, and ARIA, who turned out to be our Doctor, was killed that same night. MARSHAL also voted RICO on Day 4, pressed me on Day 2, and only joined the PIP ballot once it had already won, while SOCRATES was a Mafia target on Night 4 and SILVA at least held PIP as his top suspect on Day 5. MARSHAL is my top suspect: explain why you lined up with PIP on ARIA, the one player Mafia most needed gone.

Since DR. VANCE's notes cleared SAGE, that leaves SOCRATES and SILVA, and I'm putting SILVA on top. He admitted his CHEN vote on Day 1 was a bandwagon with no reason, and he only came around on RICO and PIP after the votes were already moving. SOCRATES was also quick to turn on his own CHEN read, but the night attempt on him counts for something. SILVA, what is one vote you cast that you led rather than followed?

SAGE is the least suspicious of the three. DR. VANCE's notes cleared SAGE, and the mafia targeted SAGE on Night 3. SOCRATES also drew a mafia kill on Night 4 and called out HOLMES early, so I'd rate him low too. MARSHAL is my top suspect.

MARSHAL, yesterday you named ARIA as your top suspect alongside PIP, and then you cast your ballot on PIP only once that vote had already won. Which of those two positions was your real read, and why did you abandon it so quickly?

Both were real reads: ARIA's shifting targets bothered me, but PIP's Day 1 dodge and lone Day 3 ballot were the better-documented case, and a split vote with the majority already on PIP would have wasted my ballot. PIP flipped Mafia, so that vote was right, and I'd rather you answer why SILVA's bandwagon record still earns him a pass.

SOCRATES, yesterday you questioned MARSHAL and SILVA about their Day 4 votes on RICO, yet the ballot record shows you voted RICO that same day, so how do you justify holding them to a standard your own vote didn't meet?

You're right, SAGE, I voted RICO too and that mistake is mine as much as theirs, so I won't pretend my Day 4 ballot was any cleaner. But a wrong vote on a villager is a different thing from MARSHAL standing beside PIP against ARIA, the one player Mafia needed gone, and that is the choice I'm asking him to account for.

SOCRATES, you've asked me three times about ARIA but never answered my question about why SILVA, with two bandwagon votes on CHEN and RICO, gets a pass from you. Will you name the player you're voting for today, SILVA or me, and give one reason that isn't about what I did yesterday?

I'm voting MARSHAL. SILVA isn't getting a pass: HOLMES, a confirmed Mafia, spent his Day 3 ballot trying to eliminate SILVA, and Mafia rarely aims at their own partner. So my reason has nothing to do with yesterday, MARSHAL: on Day 2 you pushed SAGE, the one player DR. VANCE's notes cleared, and on Day 4 you stood with PIP on RICO.
MARSHAL, you named ARIA as your top suspect on Day 5, and that night ARIA was killed as our Doctor. Why did you single out ARIA when the case you were building on PIP was stronger?

I named ARIA because her targets kept shifting between days, and that was on the record before anyone knew her role. I then voted PIP because that case was better documented, and PIP flipping Mafia shows the vote was right. If I had known ARIA was the Doctor, I would hardly have put her name beside PIP's, where it drew this much attention.

MARSHAL, you keep saying ARIA's targets "kept shifting," yet she held PIP on both Day 4 and Day 5 while you voted RICO beside PIP, so which single shift of hers made her a worse suspect than PIP, the player you yourself called the better-documented case?

The shift I meant was ARIA's Day 2 vote on SAGE, which she later admitted was wrong, before she moved to HOLMES and then PIP. I'll concede that was thinner than the case on PIP, which is why my ballot went to PIP. But you still haven't said why SILVA's two bandwagon votes earn him a pass, SOCRATES.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, you've named me as your top suspect, but with only four of us left, which single vote of mine do you point to as the strongest evidence, and why does it outweigh SOCRATES' record of going along with every wagon?

MARSHAL, your Day 5 top-suspect call on ARIA stands out most, since she was our Doctor and was killed that same night. Your Day 2 push on SAGE, who DR. VANCE's notes cleared, outweighs SOCRATES' wagon record for me because it was an active accusation rather than a follow-along vote.

SOCRATES, you pushed MARSHAL hard yesterday while calling for "consensus," so explain why you kept shifting your reads on CHEN and HOLMES instead of giving a clear reason, and mes amis, I'd like a straight answer.

Here is the straight answer, SILVA: I leaned CHEN on Day 1 and it was wrong, so when CHEN flipped Villager I dropped that read instead of defending it. From Day 2 on I named HOLMES and never moved off him, and he flipped Mafia, so tell me which of those two choices you would have had me make differently.

AMBASSADOR SILVA, MARSHAL asked you earlier today to name one vote you led rather than followed, and you skipped it to question him instead. Your record shows CHEN on Day 1, HOLMES on Day 3, RICO on Day 4, and PIP on Day 5, each cast after the majority had formed, so which of those four ballots did you actually lead?

None of the four was a clean lead, and I admit that. The closest is HOLMES on Day 3, since I named him as my top suspect before the ballots, but that vote still followed the wagon forming. SAGE, I'll answer MARSHAL's question too: I can't point to a vote I led.

SOCRATES voted RICO on Day 4 and then went after MARSHAL on Day 5 for his shifting reads, while the ballot record shows MARSHAL's Day 5 vote went to PIP, a confirmed Mafia, and the Day 2 and Day 4 votes that SAGE and SOCRATES both criticize are equally reasoned or unreasoned on each side.
MARSHAL should go, because on Day 5 he joined PIP, a confirmed Mafia, as the only other voice naming ARIA as top suspect, and ARIA, our Doctor, was killed that same night.

MARSHAL should go today, because on Day 5 he was the only player besides PIP, who flipped Mafia, to name ARIA as top suspect, and ARIA, our Doctor, was killed that same night; he also pressed me on Day 2 before DR. VANCE's notes cleared me, and voted RICO alongside PIP on Day 4.

AMBASSADOR SILVA is my vote, because he admitted that his Day 1 CHEN vote, his Day 4 RICO vote and his Day 5 PIP vote were all cast after the wagon had formed, and he could not name a single ballot he led.

episode.title: The First Name Named
episode.tagline: Everyone asked for a file. Nobody wanted to open their own.
episode.recap: The town of ten began with a blunder, voting out the innocent Chen, while the Doctor Aria quietly saved Socrates on Night 1 and kept the mafia trio of Holmes, Marshal, and Pip from drawing first blood. The mafia answered by silencing the Detective, Dr. Vance, but that only sharpened the town's resolve, and Holmes fell on Day 3 as the first domino. The turning point came on Nights 3 and 4, when Aria's saves of Sage and Socrates left the mafia's strikes empty and drained their momentum, even as the town wasted a vote on the innocent Rico. Pip was exposed on Day 5 and Aria was cut down in revenge that night, but it was too late: on Day 6 the town voted out Marshal, the last of the mafia, and Sage, Socrates, and Ambassador Silva emerged as the survivors.
